# Review

## Outcome

**Request Changes**

## Evidence

- Reviewed the implementation diff in `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/microfauna.rs`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs`, and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/habitat_biomass_pools.rs`.
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test habitat_biomass_pools -- --nocapture` passed all 10 new habitat-pool tests.
- `cargo test -p tank_core save_load_with_active_cycle_state -- --nocapture` passed.
- Custom stdin-compiled reproduction against the current build showed that after clearing plants/substrate/filter and calling `refresh_habitat_registry()`, zero-area habitats still retained non-zero biomass: `FilterMedia area=0.0 peri=0.01000 decomp=0.04000`, `PlantSurfaces area=0.0 peri=0.03000 decomp=0.00500`, `SubstrateSurface area=0.0 peri=0.06000 decomp=0.03000`, `SubstrateDeep area=0.0 decomp=0.01500`.
- Custom stdin-compiled reproduction of `tank_core::systems::nitrogen_cycle::step_nitrogen_cycle` with `DO=0` and an uneven decomposer split (`0.09 g` filter, `0.01 g` glass) produced `biomass_delta_g=-0.00008000` while total budgets increased by `delta_n_mg=0.00331034` and `delta_c_mg=0.02068966`, confirming a conservation error in the zero-effective-biomass fallback path.

## Findings and Gaps

- High: `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:258-286` only backfills habitat maps when they are empty. Because `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:424-462` seeds all habitats by default, removing a habitat later does not clear or redistribute its biomass. A glass-only tank can still carry filter/plant/substrate periphyton and decomposers, so the new pools are not actually tied to habitat availability as required.
- High: `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:252-280` routes the full aggregate decomposer decay to dissolved organics, but when `total_effective_biomass <= EPSILON` it subtracts only `decomp_decay / n` from each habitat and clamps at zero. With uneven habitat biomass this under-removes live biomass and creates nitrogen/carbon mass.
- Medium: Habitat-aware grazing is still not implemented. `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/microfauna.rs:58-64` and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:164-173` explicitly apply proportional removal across all habitats via `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/src/systems/microfauna.rs:152-162`, and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/habitat_biomass_pools.rs:229-283` only checks that total/glass biomass decrease. That does not satisfy the reviewer-specified grazing requirement that accessible surfaces be favored over filter media.

## Follow-up and Amendments

- On habitat refresh, normalize the habitat maps against the current registry: zero or remove zero-area habitats, redistribute legacy totals when habitat availability changes, and add a regression test that clearing filter/plants/substrate leaves only glass with non-zero pools.
- Fix the zero-effective decomposer fallback to distribute decay in proportion to current habitat biomass (or otherwise route only the actually removed biomass), then add a conservation regression covering `DO=0` with an uneven habitat split.
- Implement real habitat-weighted grazing for shrimp and microfauna, or explicitly rescope the bead; in either case, replace the current grazing test with one that proves filter-media periphyton loses less biomass than glass/substrate under the same grazing event.
